recommendations.text: Receive the information.

Agrees to continue using Stage 3 of the Southern Landfill within its existing footprint; to access up to approximately 170;000 tonnes of additional disposal airspace under the consent extended to 6 September 2029. This is instead of commencing use of SLEPO Cells 1 and 2 from 1 January 2028.

Agrees to undertake capital works at Stage 3 of the Southern Landfill to create the additional airspace and reduce the risk of flooding and leachate release if the Carey's Gully tunnel becomes blocked. The works comprise a reinforced concrete-faced toe bund; erosion protection and drainage improvements; upgraded debris screening; and waterproofing.

Approves unbudgeted funding of up to $5.5 million; funded through debt; for the design and construction of the Stage 3 extension and resilience works; noting that the release is subject to approval of the Project Brief and Business Case by the project SRO; in accordance with the Council's Investment Delivery Framework.
Agrees the funding is phased as follows:
FY26/27: $1.5 million ($130;000 opex for detailed design and the business case; and $1.37 million capex)
FY27/28: $4.0 million

decisions.title: 2027-37 LTP - Capital programme recommendations from the Revenue and Financial Value Review (RFVR) Working Group
decisions.summary: The purpose of this report is for Ngā Kaihoe Pūtea | Revenue and Financial Value Review Working Group (the Working Group) to make recommendations to Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee (the Committee) on current capital programmes and potential future options to address the in-principle financial parameters set for the 2027-37 Long-term Plan (LTP).
decisions.mataiUrl: https://meetings.wellington.govt.nz/your-council/reports/2106/2027-37 LTP - Capital programme recommendations from the Revenue and Financial Value Review (RFVR) Working Group
decisions.reportUrl: https://meetings.wellington.govt.nz/your-council/reports/2106/2027-37 LTP - Capital programme recommendations from the Revenue and Financial Value Review (RFVR) Working Group
relatedReports: Ngā Kaihoe Pūtea | Revenue and Financial Value Review Working Group standing oral update
Ngā Kaihoe Pūtea | Revenue and Financial Value Review Working Group standing oral update

recommendations.text: Receive the information.

Note that for Wellington City Council to achieve the 4 percent average rates increase limit set in principle for 2027-37 Long-term Plan; savings and efficiencies need to be developed that can be included in the December 2026 Long-term Plan budget deliberations.
Adopt the key principle that existing infrastructure is prioritised across all business units within the Long-term Plan.
Adopt the principle that the renewal of infrastructure will also consider renewals that seek to reduce operating costs.
Adopt the principle that development contributions/levies adequately contribute to the Council’s cost of growth.
Note that significant parts of the Capital Programme require updated 10-year funding projections.
Request updated funding projections are brought back to the Working Group for a final review of Capex to inform December.

Agree that the proposed capital expenditure changes identified in this report and Attachment 1 from the second tranche of measures to be reflected in the draft 2027–37 Long-term Plan budget; with Ngā Kaihoe Pūtea | Revenue and Financial Value Review Working Group to undertake further work ahead of the December’s budget deliberations to support development of a draft 2027-37 Long-term Plan budget that meets the financial parameters agreed in principle by the Committee; including
options for Council expenditure to inform recommendations for inclusion in the Revenue and Financing Policy;
additional information arising from recommendations
cost-efficiency and effectiveness reviews; formerly known as section 17A reviews; and
any other matters arising from the Committee’s deliberations that fall within the delegations of the Working Group
To receive a report-back from officers on savings relating to:
UP1 Urban Planning; Heritage and Public Spaces Development: Removing unallocated Central City Framework funding
TN4 Transport Network: Remove unallocated City Streets funding in time for December 2026 Long-term Plan budget considerations; and
PB3 Parks; Beaches and Open Space: Removing $21.4m of funding for the Chinese Garden Project and Fale Malae
Request officers extensively explore funding; ownership and strengthening options relating to the Council’s earthquake-prone buildings; and

Note that estimated earthquake strengthening costs of $300m for key buildings through the Long-term Plan would put at risk the ability for the Council to deliver on core infrastructure needs; particularly within a rates capping environment.

Note that an aligned earthquake strengthening budget line will be created that incorporates LU 2038 Gallery & Museum Upgrades (Bond Store funding) with CR 2128 Civic Campus and Resilience Improvements (Michael Fowler Centre funding).

Agree that the Long-term Plan make the future of earthquake prone buildings a key proposal for consultation with the public; including options to explore the preference of what venues are priority for strengthening
For LU 2151 Te Awe Mapara
Agree for officers to decouple the following projects into individual project lines and provide suggested phasing
Central pools / major aquatic intervention
Northern recreation centre
Tawa facility intervention
Newtown facility intervention
Kilbirnie facility intervention

Agree; based on the principles set out in recommendation 3 and 4; that the relevant committee receives advice on renewal/upgrades to Thorndon and Freyberg Pools verses the construction of a new Pool (as per the current scope within Te Awe Mapara) and makes an in-principle decision on how to proceed

Agree that the Northern Recreation Centre project retain funding of $5m for early planning works. Additional funding will be considered in a subsequent Long-term Plan in response to future population growth.
Agree that any residual Te Awe Mapara funding after recommendations 11.1 to 11.3 are taken into account is removed from the budget.

Agree the proposed additional capital programme savings and budget variances as detailed in Attachment 1 to be reflected in the draft capital budget for consideration at the December 2026 draft 2027-37 Long-term Plan budget deliberations:

Parks; Beaches and Open Space: PB1- Remove Planned Property Purchases – Reserves and Town Belt & Reserves budget relating to purchase of additional green space. Future purchases presented to council as opportunities arise.
Parks; Beaches and Open Space - PB2 - Note $2.47m saving for Huetepara Park as now funded by WIAL.

Parks; Beaches and Open Space - PB3 - Remove $18.4m of funding for the Chinese Garden Project and Fale Malae but retain $3m of funding for resource consenting. Briefing requested on project status for early 2027.
12.4 - City Promotions and Business Support - CP1 - Rephase Wellington Venues renewals to match review underway.
Recreation Facilities and Services - RF1 - Rescope playground renewals and upgrades to only include new playgrounds if funded mainly by Development Contributions.
Recreation Facilities and Services - RF2 - Remove funding for the Northern Suburbs Recreation Centre from Recreation Centre Renewal as duplicate budget with Te Awe Mapara.
Community Facilities and Services - CF1 - Include the planned Capex requirements for libraries within the Cost Efficiency and Effectiveness review of Libraries.
Community Facilities and Services - CF2 - Include the planned Capex requirements for community facilities in the Cost Efficiency and Effectiveness review of Community Centres and Halls
Community Facilities and Services - CF3 - Rephase public convenience and pavilion (toilet) funding to match updated growth needs.
Urban Planning; Heritage and Public Spaces Development - UP1 - Remove unallocated Central City Framework funding.
Urban Planning; Heritage and Public Spaces Development - UP2 - Remove funding for Minor CBD Enhancements in 2033/34.
Transport Network - TN1 - Request details of the rates-funded component of new roads; and review the accounting treatment of developer-gifted roads
Transport Network TN2 Request CP&F Committee review current phasing within the Long-term Plan of new cycleways.
Transport Network - TN3 - Combine budgets for Footpath renewals and Pedestrian Network accessways.
Transport Network - TN4 - Remove unallocated City Streets funding
Parking - PK1 - Rescope Parking Asset Renewals to exclude parking meter upgrades in later years of the Long-term Plan.
Organisation - OG1 - Remove Business Unit Support as a Capex and treat I.C.T. as Opex (software as a service); while continuing to debt fund.
Organisation - OG2 - Reduce the Capital Replacement Fund to match historic spend and combine with Health and Safety – Legislation Compliance.
Organisation - OG3 - Review the Civic Property Renewals and Commercial Properties Renewals budgets.
Request officers to report back to the Working Group on the following ahead of December deliberations:
Officers to prioritise Capex proposals by CCOs for further consideration by the Working Group; including consideration of invest-to-earn revenue implications.
Officers to investigate removal of residential housing assets within CR2004 Parks Buildings where cost savings can be made and report back to CP&F on options.
Officers to reported back to the relevant committee on the renewal of HUP1 assets within CR 2060 Housing Renewals (approx. $90m) and ensure the cost assumptions are thoroughly interrogated.

Endorse increased renewal funding for LU 2083 Wall Upgrades to LU 2089 Roading Capacity Upgrades to better cope with extreme weather events and build greater city resilience and request a report back on LU2104 Rural Roading
Note this is to be included in the report back to the WG on the decision on 22 October relating to resilience and hazard funding.
Officers to prepare a budget paper covering service levels; identified needs and required spending for Minor Works Improvements under LU 2105 Safety Upgrades.
Officers provide Information on the funding allocation for Cuba St within LU 2141 LGWM – City Streets.
Officers to conduct a thorough review of budgets relating to CR 2119 Civic Property Renewals and CR 2120 Commercial Properties Renewals as per the principles set out in recommendation 3 and 4

Note that for areas where recommendations are not progressed and where changes have not been considered; the draft Long-term Plan budget for December will reflect the current capital programme arrangements and funding levels
Note that the RFVWG considered capital programme savings for the current year (2026/27) and recommendations on these will come through to this committee through a separate paper.
Note Officers are to report back to the relevant committee on the renewal of HUP1 assets within CR 2060 Housing Renewals (approx. $90m) and ensure the cost assumptions are thoroughly interrogated.

Endorse increased renewal funding for LU 2083 Wall Upgrades to LU 2089 Roading Capacity Upgrades to better cope with extreme weather events and build greater city resilience and request a report back on LU2104 Rural Roading.
Note this is to be included in the report back to the WG on the decision on 22 October relating to resilience and hazard funding.

amendments.text: Request the Chief Executive to prepare high-level advice and high-level indicative costings for specific capital projects to be considered at the deliberations currently scheduled for 10 December 2026:
All commitments in Mahere Tautoru Triennium Plan 2025-2028 that remain to be delivered

Options to change the design and operation of approximately 170m of the Glenmore Street cycleway; to address community concerns about access by elderly and disabled people to the Begonia House; Lady Norwood Rose Garden and Soundshell;
Options to change Cambridge and Kent Terrace bus lanes to part-time operation during weekday peak hours

Options and costings for capital investment in emergency preparedness; including ‘Day 1’ community hubs and Emergency Assistance Centres; and temporary flood barriers and associated flood-response equipment
Options for a basic fit-out on the ground floor of the St James to be used as an exhibition space as part of inner-city revitalisation
Options to address deferred maintenance on the St James roof to address leaks;
Options for a new off leash dog park in the Mt Cook area;
Bringing Freyberg and Thorndon Pools into the electrification programme; and bringing forward the Wellington Regional Aquatic Centre electrification by one year
Establishing a flood resilience work programme; having regard to the Apri 2026 flooding even
Rainwater retention at sports fields and community facilities
Dedicated funding for solar panel and battery installation at council facilities;
Dedicated funding for the EV First Fleet programme (if and where CAPEX is required);
Contingency for basic infrastructure at Mātai Moana; in particular public toilets; staff facilities and signage

Advice on options to deliver a programme of capital works to stop leachate from old landfills entering the stormwater network and being discharged into the Houghton Bay marine reserve; informed by contemporary reporting by GWRC; and noting that Tiaki Wai now has responsibility for stormwater but managing old landfills remains a council responsibility

A Northland Village Upgrade Project; including design work and improvements to village amenities and the transport corridor for safer connections between the local shops; community centre and school; valued at no more than $3m;

Options to refine approximately 200m of the Ngaio Connections cycleway on Kaiwharawhara Road; including reinstating the 4-7pm clearway to restore on-street parking for Kaiwharawhara business district businesses; valued at no more than $100k;

Options to refine approximately 200m of the Karori Connections cycleway at Karori Park; including peak-time cycleway operation to enable off-peak on-street parking during busy sportsfield and playground use; valued at no more than $100k;
Retaining $2.1m in the Footpath Upgrades budget to deliver the Onslow Road footpath; for which design is underway;
Restoration of the Wrights Hill fortress area; including maintaining the surrounding access road; valued at no more than $200;000
An Ian Galloway Park upgrade; including floodlighting and an artificial turf field at ‘the Cage’ to address the shortage of pitches in the west; valued at no more than $3m;

Ring-fenced funding of approximately $100;000–$200;000 for emergency preparedness in Ohariu Valley and Horokiwi; including support for Ohariu Hall to operate as a community emergency hub (such as signage; solar power; a generator; water and septic systems and satellite communications); and a storage container for Horokiwi;
feasibility study and business case for a Johnsonville recreation centre; including demand; facility options; partnerships; costs and operating implications;
Options and costings for a targeted package of improvements to the Newlands shopping centre and surrounding public spaces; such as streetscape works; seating and planting;
Development of a business case for a Tawa anchor project; including advice on whether it is capital or operating expenditure;
ptions to redirect funding from the planned Middleton Road cycleway to address high-risk tree and road-safety issues at Glenside and Middleton Roads more quickly and at a lower cost.
Options and costings to accelerate the replacement of uncovered Council-owned bus shelters with covered shelters; initially focusing on inbound stops;
ptions for a suburban centre upgrade for Johnsonville including provision of green space by retaining and repurposing $1.3m from the sale of the Old Johnsonville Library site;

Delivering the Island Bay Library Car Park version 2 business case; to maintain public confidence in Wellington City Council by fulfilling the commitment made at the Environment and Infrastructure Committee of 5 December 2024;
Options for a suburban centre upgrade for Newtown
A purpose-built outdoor calisthenics facility similar to the Pirie Street Calisthenics Park and Play Area; in the Paekawakawa / Southern General Ward at or near Newtown
Options for outdoor shelter; or redevelopment to increase internal space at Raukawa Community Centre;

Options to further increase the provision of assistive equipment (and any associated inclusive design elements) at key outdoor locations; such as beach wheelchairs and accessible matting in line with recommendations in Tātou ki Uta - Coastal Reserves Management Plan (2025); recommendations from the Disabled Communities Advisory Group; and recommendations following the pilot program at Freyberg Beach;

Options to protect or enhance habitat for indigenous ground nesting sea and shore birds such as penguin friendly infrastructure or penguin-friendly nest boxes in line with recommendations in Tātou ki Uta - Coastal Reserves Management Plan (2025);
Options for minor CAPEX support or amenities for unhoused people such as recommendations in Te Awe Māpara Community Facilities Plan (2023) for facilities such as public showers
Options for a targeted increase in bilingual and bicultural signage; including street signage and cultural interpretation signage;
Safer pedestrian crossing at the intersection of Abel St and Cuba Streets.
Retaining approximately $1.6m in the sportsfield renewals programme to deliver a renewal of the Newtown Park athletic track;
Retaining approximately $2.9m in the sportsfield renewals programme for a renewal of the Wakefield Park artificial turfs and shockpads;
Retaining existing parks-building renewal funding for key Southern Ward operational assets; including the Newtown Operations Depot.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.

Agrees to continue using Stage 3 of the Southern Landfill within its existing footprint; to access up to approximately 170;000 tonnes of additional disposal airspace under the consent extended to 6 September 2029. This is instead of commencing use of SLEPO Cells 1 and 2 from 1 January 2028.

Agrees to undertake capital works at Stage 3 of the Southern Landfill to create the additional airspace and reduce the risk of flooding and leachate release if the Carey's Gully tunnel becomes blocked. Y26/27: $1.5 million ($130;000 opex for detailed design and the business case; and $1.37 million capex)
FY27/28: $4.0 million

decisions.title: Extending the City Safety and Wellbeing Plan - options for a place based suburban safety response
decisions.summary: This report presents options for extending the City Safety and Wellbeing Plan into suburban centres; starting with Newtown; in response to Triennium Plan Commitment 68. It seeks the Committee’s agreement on a preferred service model to inform the 2027–37 Long-term Plan deliberations; including the additional investment required to support a place-based suburban response while maintaining the existing CBD service
decisions.mataiUrl: https://meetings.wellington.govt.nz/your-council/reports/2102/Extending the City Safety and Wellbeing Plan - options for a place based suburban safety response
decisions.reportUrl: https://meetings.wellington.govt.nz/your-council/reports/2102/Extending the City Safety and Wellbeing Plan - options for a place based suburban safety response
relatedReports: City Safety and Wellbeing Plan

recommendations.text: Note the evidence and lessons from the CBD city safety response and Newtown Safety Project that inform the proposed place-based approach to suburban safety.
Agree that any suburban extension of the City Safety and Wellbeing Plan should be separately resourced and maintain the existing CBD level of service.

Agree that Option 2 - maintaining the existing CBD service and establishing one additional; flexible place-based suburban capability; commencing in Newtown and able to scale or shift according to evidence; risk and local need; is the preferred model for consideration through the 2027–37 Long-term Plan deliberations.

Note that the indicative additional funding requirements for Option 2 comprise: • approximately $555;000 per annum for Council staffing and associated operating costs; Page 60 Item 2.2 • up to approximately $200;000 per annum for locally appropriate partner contracts or targeted grants; bringing the combined indicative operating requirement to up to approximately $755;000 per annum; and • an indicative capital allowance of approximately $200;000 per annum for the first two years for CCTV; lighting and other Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design (CPTED) or place-based safety improvements; with specific investments determined through local safety planning and site-specific assessment.
Note that the additional funding identified above is not provided within existing budgets; and implementation of Option 2 would be subject to funding approval through the 2027–37 Long-term Plan.

Note that the attached Newtown; Johnsonville and Kilbirnie place profiles provide an initial evidence base for local safety planning and illustrate the proposed assessment approach; these do not commit Council to a particular service level or investment in each location.

Direct the Chief Executive to ensure all practicable steps are taken to ensure council and relevant external agencies; including Wellington Electricity; are responding with appropriate priority to installation of lighting; giving particular priority to the installation of lighting in the Wilson St parking area in Newtown noting the budget for this was approved in March 2026.

Agree that subject to 2027–37 Long-term Plan final deliberations; the final service design for Option 2; informed by engagement between officers; Councillors; the local community and local social service providers; be brought back to the Committee for approval prior to implementation.

amendments.text: Request that in engagements with Central Government the Mayor will advocate on behalf of the city for Police to be resourced and empowered to enforce the law; Health and Social Services be funded to address the drivers of crime; and that Ministers fulfil their responsibilities for keeping Wellingtonians safe; rather than expecting ratepayers to fill the gaps while constraining Council through the proposed rates-capping.

decisions.summary: Direction is sought on recycling service levels and funding; and the scale; pace and priorities of waste minimisation investment for inclusion in the draft 2027–37 Long-term Plan. recommendations.text: Receive the information.

Agrees to include the Transitional Recycling Funding Model (Option R2) for consideration as part of the 2027-37 Long-term Plan process; which comprises:
Waste minimisation levy fund revenue of $1.5m per annum;
Increased recycling levy
Agrees to include the Invest and Prepare Investment Scenario (Option I2) for consideration as part of the 2027-37 Long-term Plan process.
Agrees that Investment Scenario 2 (Option I2) comprises Council funding the following initiatives
Core Programme
Waste Minimisation Staff & Work Programme - 1A - Retain current staffing and work program allocation - Each year of LTP $1;000;000
WMMP program - 2A - Retain allocation for WMMP program of work - Each year of LTP $500;000
Initial Investment Options
Community and Local Organics Trial - 5A - Diverse & Distributed Organics Network Trial - 27/28: $585;000 Further four years ending 31/32: $500;000 per year
Transfer Station changes - 6C - Incremental improvements - 27/28: $145;000 Further four years ending 31/32: $70;000 per year
Construction and Demolition - 7A - Construction and Demolition Trial at the Landfill - 27/28: $70;000 28/29: $70;000
Resource Recovery Network Expansion 8A - Community Recovery Network & Pop-up Collection Trial - $100;000 for four years starting 27/28 and ending 30/31.
Central City Resource Recovery / Te Aro Zero Waste - 9D - Retain funding and procure - $250;000 for three years starting 28/29 and ending 30/31
5.2.6 Supporting Wellington’s Repair Sector - 10A - Voucher scheme - repair vouchers to be redeemed at participating repair businesses - $100;000 for four years starting 27/28 and ending 30/31.
Longer Term Investment Options
Tipshop Upgrades - 13A - Tipshop Upgrades Business case and capex - 30/31: $100;000 business case 31/32: $2.4m capex
Future Waste Pathways - 18A - Future Waste Pathways Initiatives - Business case and capex - $250;000 for two years ending 28/29. 30/31: $5m capex
Notes that Council adopted the Zero Waste Strategy in April 2023; establishing a long-term direction and targets towards a low-waste; circular economy.

Notes that the current waste funding and operating model is under increasing pressure; particularly in relation to recycling services; and that further work is required to identify sustainable long-term funding and operating models which will be considered through future Annual Plan and Long-term Plan processes.
Notes that Council is forecast to receive approximately $4.5 million per annum in Waste Minimisation Levy funding and currently holds approximately $9 million in accumulated levy reserves.

Notes that; after allowing for existing programme commitments and recycling support; approximately $1.5 million per annum of further annual levy funding is available for new waste minimisation investment without drawing on accumulated reserves

Notes that significant local and regional work is underway; including the Future Waste Pathways programme; which may materially influence future waste infrastructure; services; investment priorities and funding requirements.
Notes that the transitional funding model (Option R2) is intended to be a short-term approach while a new financial model for recycling is developed.

recommendations.text: Receive the information

Note that for Wellington City Council to achieve the 4 percent average rates increase limit set in principle for 2027-37 Long-term Plan; savings and efficiencies need to be developed that can be included in the December 2026 Long-term Plan budget deliberations.

that Parliament has completed the first reading of legislation to implement a rates capping regime with an initial target range of 2 to 4 percent; that councils will be required to have regard to the target range for the 2027/28 and 2028/29 financial years; and that the proposed legislation requires the 2027–37 Long-term Plan comply with the target range for the 2029/30 year and in each year thereafter; unless an exemption applies;

that the Minister of Local Government has written to councils setting out his expectation that the 2027–37 Long-term Plans will be prepared consistently with the intent of the proposed rates capping legislation;

the Committee’s 25 June 2026 in-principle agreement to the strategic direction and community outcomes for the 2027–37 Long-term Plan and the key financial parameters underpinning the draft Financial Strategy; including a debt-to-revenue ratio limit of 200 percent and a rates increase limit of 4 percent per annum;
that; following this meeting; Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee will deliberate on the draft 2027-37 Long-term Plan budget and options for consultation in December 2026.
Officers will then prepare the 2027-37 Long-term Plan Consultation Document (including consultation options) for consideration by committee and approval for audit in February.

decisions.title: Procurement Framework Refresh
decisions.summary: The purpose of this report is to present the draft Wellington City Council Procurement Strategy and Operational Procurement Policy to Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee (the Committee) and seek adoption of the documents; subject to any amendments arising from Committee feedback.
relatedReports: Mahere Tautoru | Triennium Plan 2025 - 2028 Recommendation to Adopt

additionalDocuments.name: THIS MEETING'S START TIME HAS CHANGED

recommendations.text: Receive the information.

Note that the draft Wellington City Council Procurement framework; consisting of the Procurement Strategy; Operational Procurement Policy and Contract Management Policy have been reviewed; with substantial updates to the Procurement Strategy & Operational Procurement Policy.
Adopt the Policy framework documents; including the Procurement Strategy; Operational Procurement Policy and Contract Management Policy.
Delegate to the Chair of the Council Planning and Finance Committee and Chief Executive the authority to make any minor editorial changes arising from Committee feedback.

amendments.text: Adopt the Policy framework documents; including the Procurement Strategy; Operational Procurement Policy and Contract Management Policy; with the following changes:
Add an appendix to the Operational Procurement Policy; which will identify and define service areas to be brought to Te Taurapa | Council Planning Finance Committee for approval.

Add to the Procurement Strategy “Periodically assess contracts falling within service areas identified in the appendix; but no later than 12 months before the end of contract and/or commencement of a procurement process; to determine whether the current delivery model remains the most appropriate approach; recognising the Council’s preference for in-house delivery; where possible.”

Note that prior to a procurement process commencing; Te Taurapa | Council Planning Finance Committee will receive officer advice and make decisions about the service delivery model for service areas listed in the appendix outlined in 3.2.
Request the Chief Executive report back to Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee with the proposed appendix outlined in 3.1; which should:
include contracts; services and projects of strategic; financial; operational or community importance;
include; at a minimum; service arrangements with whole of life expenditure exceeding $20 million; and
identify other long-term service contracts that officers consider strategic due to their scale; duration; criticality; public interest or impact on organisational capability.

Add the following Guiding Principle to the Procurement Strategy: “Public Benefit: Council will protect and enhance public confidence; organisational capability and long term service effectiveness by ensuring strategic services are periodically reviewed to confirm the delivery model remains appropriate and continues to deliver value for money and service outcomes.”

Note that the United Nations Human Rights Council publishes a database that it reviews and updates regularly of business enterprises involved in specified activities related to illegal Israeli settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.

Note that officers have reviewed the Council's current supplier arrangements and have identified one entity connected to the United Nations Human Rights Council database and council encourages the chief executive to address that situation as and when prudent.

Recommend that Council direct officers not to procure goods or services from entities identified on the United Nations Human Rights Council database; without the approval of the Chief Executive who should notify the Mayor about any exemption approved.
Request that officers incorporate this direction into Council's procurement guidance; procedures; and supplier due diligence processes.

Request officers develop a proportionate procurement reporting framework in consultation with the independent Chair of Te Kura o te Waka | Audit and Risk Committee and the Chair of Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee. Reporting should consider including but not be limited to:
material instances of procurement or contractual non-compliance; including the nature of the issue and the corrective action being taken.

contracts awarded; including the supplier's name; contract value or value range; and a brief description of the goods; services or works procured; where publication is lawful and does not unreasonably prejudice Council’s or a supplier’s commercial interests.
consideration of alternative delivery models; including opportunities for in-house delivery where appropriate.
the number and total value of Council contracts; presented in appropriate value bands.
significant direct appointments; exemptions and departures from the Operational Procurement Policy.
significant supplier expenditure and supplier concentration; including a consolidated view of Council’s ten highest-value supplier relationships; the associated expenditure and number of contracts.
significant current and planned procurement activity; including key milestones
significant contracts expected to expire; be renewed or require a new procurement process within the following 12 to 18 months.
current and planned open-market procurement opportunities; with appropriate links or information published through the Council website and relevant procurement platforms.
actions taken to reduce unnecessary barriers to participation by new suppliers; local businesses; Māori businesses; small and medium-sized enterprises and other capable suppliers.

finalClauses.text: Receive the information.

Note that the draft Wellington City Council Procurement framework; consisting of the Procurement Strategy; Operational Procurement Policy and Contract Management Policy have been reviewed; with substantial updates to the Procurement Strategy & Operational Procurement Policy.
Adopt the Policy framework documents; including the Procurement Strategy; Operational Procurement Policy and Contract Management Policy.

decisions.title: Rating Policy Review Consultation document
decisions.summary: This report to Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee seeks approval of the consultation document on the proposed changes to the rating policies before public consultation on the 2027-37 Long-Term Plan in early 2027.
relatedReports: Proposed Rating Policy Changes for Consultation to Inform the 2027-37 LTP

recommendations.text: Receive the information.

Adopt the Consultation Document and agree that community consultation on the proposed changes to rating policies set out in it; be consulted on over a four-week period from 19 October to 15 November 2026.
Note that formal consultation on the rating policy settings will occur as part of the 2027 37 Long-term Plan consultation in March and April 2027.
Delegate to the Mayor; Chief Executive and Chair of the Council Planning and Finance Committee the authority to make any minor editorial changes that may arise as part of the publication process.

amendments.text: Adopt the Consultation Document and draft survey with the following edits and agree that community consultation on the proposed changes to rating policies set out in it; be consulted on over a four-week period from 19 October to 15 November 2026.

Add “The Productivity Commission (2015) encourages councils to consider the merits of land value rating in encouraging the efficient use of land when reviewing their rating policies. There is also evidence that land value rating is a better proxy for income than capital value.” after ‘Advocates also argue that land value rating can discourage land banking and underutilization of valuable urban land; helping to support housing development and more efficient urban growth' in paragraph 5 of page 6 of the consultation document.

Amend paragraph 6; page 6 of the consultation document to read “Advocates argue that properties with higher capital values often place greater demands on Council services and therefore capital value may provide a better indication of a property owner's ability to pay rates.

Remove "Capital values are also updated every three years; making them relatively straightforward to apply across the city; whereas land values can be more difficult to validate" from paragraph 6; page 6.

Replace "Given the uncertainty about the potential for councils in the region to amalgamate; it may not be the right time for Wellington City Council to use a different system from our neighbouring council" in paragraph 3; page 7 of the consultation document with "The potential for councils in the region to amalgamate will have an impact on the implementation and timeline for any change to the rating system."

Amend paragraph 7 on page 7 of the consultation document to read "If the Council decided to change to land value rating; there would be implementation costs which are estimated at between $600;000 to $2 million. This would be paid for through rates and would be an addition to the budget."

. Update paragraph 3; page 9 of the consultation document to read "Commercial ratepayers currently contribute 49 percent of the Council’s total rates revenue." The rationale for a higher commercial differential is three-fold. First; there is a large commuter base that comes into the City for work and uses the infrastructure (on average 38;000 commuters daily). Second; businesses can deduct GST from their rates and deduct rates from their taxable income; which is not available to residential ratepayers. Third; reducing this differential would have a substantial impact on residential ratepayers.

Amend paragraph 3; page 10 of the consultation document to read "Our proposal is to change the general rates differential for commercial; industrial and business rate payers over six years from 3.7:1 to 3.0:1. Retaining the status quo; or other differentials are also viable options."
Amend paragraph 4; page 10 of the consultation document to read "If the Council reduces the commercial rate; commercial ratepayers will pay a smaller piece of the total rates pie."

Insert new paragraph "The proposed changes aim to increase economic investment and job creation. However; it remains uncertain whether a reduction in commercial rates will be passed on by commercial landlords to businesses" following paragraph 6; page 10 of the consultation document; "This would help make it easier for ratepayers to budget for the change; instead of making it all in one year."

Amend paragraph 7; page 10 of the consultation document to read "Table 1 shows our proposed option alongside other potential options and the status quo for an average downtown commercial property and an average residential property that both have a capital value of $1.5 million. It shows the corresponding increase in residential rates for any reduction in commercial rates. "
Add new option 5 to Survey Question Q8 – P1_BENEFITS: “System is fairer / a better reflection of service consumption”
Amend Survey Question Q14 – P2_BENEFITS amend to Commercial ratepayers pay lower rates / improved commercial affordability
Add new option 3 to Survey Question Q15 – P2_CONCERNS add concern “Disproportionate benefit to commercial landlords / businesses do not receive affordability benefits”

Add to Key Proposal 1 in the consultation document “This review is considering both how rates are calculated and how rates are shared across the city. The current commercial differential of 3.7:1 operates within the existing capital value rating system. The examples in this section assume that the capital value system would continue. If the Council were to decide to change to a land value rating system; further work would be required to determine the appropriate commercial differential and how any changes should be implemented.”

Add to Key Proposal 2 in the consultation document “This review is considering both how rates are calculated and how rates are shared across the city. The current commercial differential of 3.7:1 operates within the existing capital value rating system. If the Council were to decide to change to a land value rating system; further work would be required to determine the appropriate commercial differential and how any changes should be implemented.”

Amend Table 1 in the consultation document (page 11 of the consultation document) to include; for each commercial differential option; the resulting percentage share of the general rates requirement paid by residential and commercial ratepayers.

Replace survey question Q13-P2_ALTERNATIVES “Irrespective of your views on the proposed reduction to the commercial rating differential. Would you support any of the following changes to the commercial rate differential?” with “While the Council’s preferred option is decreasing the differential to 3.0:1; other changes (or no change) are also options. Would you support any of the following changes to the commercial rate differential?” and add a new first option to Q13-P2_ALTERNATIVES “Keeping the commercial differential at 3.7:1” and remove option “I do not support any changes to the commercial differential”

finalClauses.text: Receive the information.

Adopt the Consultation Document and agree that community consultation on the proposed changes to rating policies set out in it; be consulted on over a four-week period from 19 October to 15 November 2026.
Note that formal consultation on the rating policy settings will occur as part of the 2027 37 Long-term Plan consultation in March and April 2027.

Delegate to the Mayor; Chief Executive and Chair of the Council Planning and Finance Committee the authority to make any minor editorial changes that may arise as part of the publication process and to meet the need for balance and neutrality expected of an early consultation document.

decisions.title: External Legal Advice Fund
decisions.summary: This report seeks Council decisions on the purpose of the External Legal Advice Fund and procedure for Council to access it. The fund is available to elected members to support Council and Committee decision-making.
relatedReports: Mahere Tautoru | Triennium Plan 2025 - 2028 Recommendation to Adopt

recommendations.text: Receive the information.

Note $50;000 has been budgeted within the 2026/27 Annual Plan for the External Legal Advice Fund in accordance with Outcome 4 of the Mahere Tautoru Triennium Plan 2025 2028 and will be administered through the General Counsel’s cost centre.

Note where a decision is made to use the External Legal Advice Fund; it is the Council seeking legal advice not the council organisation and it is important to maintain independence from the council organisation in the external legal advice. As such; the General Counsel will provide practical support to engage the external legal provider and ensure compliance with the council organisation’s policies and procedures relevant to procuring; paying for; keeping records of and maintaining legal privilege over external legal advice but will not otherwise be involved in reviewing or commenting on the legal advice itself.

Agree the purpose of the External Legal Advice Fund is to allow the Council to obtain external legal review of the organisation’s legal advice relating to important constitutional matters to ensure the organisation’s position does not infringe on the rights and privileges of elected members.
Agree a decision to use the External Legal Advice Fund may be made by Council or a Committee of the Whole.
there is reasonable doubt whether the Council or a Committee would be properly compliant with its statutory obligations in following the advice or accepting a recommendation based on the advice; or
there is reasonable doubt whether the Council or a Committee is acting constitutionally or in accordance with any rules or secondary legislation regulating its conduct; and
the legal or reputational risk to the Council is sufficiently material to justify seeking further assurance before a decision by Council or a Committee is made.
Agree the procedure for making a decision to use the External Legal Advice Fund as set out in this paper and with the following key elements:

Elected members who disagree with the council organisation’s legal advice should first raise their concerns or questions with the Chief Executive or General Counsel. Following that; if elected members wish to test the council organisation’s legal advice with an external review; they must consult with the Mayor and obtain the Mayor’s approval to seek a decision from Council or Committee of the Whole to use the fund.

Once the Mayor’s approval is obtained; elected members seeking a decision to use the External Legal Advice Fund should seek advice from the General Counsel; who will work with the elected member to submit a paper or make an amendment; whichever is appropriate in the circumstances.
The General Counsel may provide advice:
on whether the purpose of the fund is met; and

to ensure any recommendation or amendment includes sufficient and clear detail as to the advice sought and appropriate delegations to an elected member who can instruct and liaise with the external legal provider.
If a motion to access the External Legal Advice Fund is successful; sufficient information about the purpose and nature of the review sought must be agreed at the same meeting.

Authority to agree final instructions and to carry out all steps necessary to assist with completion of legal advice must be delegated to the Mayor or another elected member at the same meeting where the decision is made to use the External Legal Advice Fund.

The General Counsel will provide advice on appropriate external legal providers; ensure all required Legal Services Orders and Purchase Orders are created; and receive and ensure payment of invoices. The General Counsel will be provided with the final legal advice for record-keeping purposes but will otherwise not be involved in the review of or comment on draft legal advice.
Note that the General Counsel may assist with administrative actions to ensure a decision in accordance with this policy is carried out.

finalClauses.text: Receive the information.

Note $50;000 has been budgeted within the 2026/27 Annual Plan for the External Legal Advice Fund in accordance with Outcome 4 of the Mahere Tautoru Triennium Plan 2025 2028 and will be administered through the General Counsel’s cost centre.

Agree that in the event elected members disagree with advice provided by the General Counsel (whether it is legal advice prepared by the General Counsel or by external legal counsel on the instruction of the General Counsel) on a matter before the Council or a Committee; members will; in the first instance; raise their concerns and questions with the Chief Executive or General Counsel to seek clarification of the advice or to ascertain whether the concerns or questions of elected members warrant reconsideration of the advice provided.

Agree that in the event that disagreement with the advice remains following an approach to the Chief Executive or General Counsel; those elected members may consider using the External Legal Advice Fund to obtain a second legal opinion.

Agree that the External Legal Advice Fund may be used when; following legal advice provided by the General Counsel (whether it is legal advice prepared by the General Counsel or by external legal counsel on the instruction of the General Counsel) in relation to a matter before the Council or a Committee; a majority of Council determine:
there is reasonable doubt whether the Council or a Committee would be properly compliant with its statutory obligations in following the advice or accepting a recommendation based on the advice; or
there is reasonable doubt whether the Council or a Committee is acting constitutionally or in accordance with any rules or secondary legislation regulating its conduct; and
the legal or reputational risk to the Council is sufficiently material to justify seeking further assurance before a decision by Council or a Committee is made.
Agree that in the event a majority of Council determines there are grounds to seek alternative legal advice; they will then:
determine the legal question on which advice is being sought;
agree on a factual statement setting out the background to the legal question;
identify a relevant legal service provider from the All of Government Panel of Legal Service Providers from which to seek advice;
on whether the purpose of the fund is met; and

to ensure any recommendation or amendment includes sufficient and clear detail as to the advice sought and appropriate delegations to an elected member who can instruct and liaise with the external legal provider.
instruct the Mayor to prepare and convey a letter of instruction in accordance with the decisions of the majority of Council.

Authority to agree final instructions and to carry out all steps necessary to assist with completion of legal advice must be delegated to the Mayor or another elected member at the same meeting where the decision is made to use the External Legal Advice Fund.

The General Counsel will provide advice on appropriate external legal providers; ensure all required Legal Services Orders and Purchase Orders are created; and receive and ensure payment of invoices. The General Counsel will be provided with the final legal advice for record-keeping purposes but will otherwise not be involved in the review of or comment on draft legal advice.
Note that the General Counsel may assist with administrative actions to ensure a decision in accordance with this policy is carried out.

decisions.summary: This report seeks approval from the Te Hoe Matua | City Strategy and Delivery Committee for an interim safety improvement at the Courtenay Place; Cambridge Terrace and Kent Terrace intersection (Golden Mile Work Package 1). The recommendation is to install a temporary pedestrian connection to improve safety and reduce informal crossing movements while longer-term decisions for Courtenay Place are progressed.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.

Endorse Option 2 as the preferred interim make-safe treatment for Golden Mile Work Package 1; being the installation of a temporary pedestrian connection between the median footpath and the existing signalised crossing at the Courtenay Place / Cambridge Terrace / Kent Terrace intersection.

Note that Option 2 is recommended because it addresses the immediate safety and accessibility issue created by the current layout; reduces informal pedestrian movements through the cycleway corridor and around barriers; improves legibility and wayfinding for people walking through the intersection; and retains flexibility while longer-term Courtenay Place network decisions are developed.

Note that the temporary connection is expected to be in place for approximately 12 18 months; can be delivered within the funding retained for Work Package 1 make-safe works; and does not pre-determine future decisions for Courtenay Place or the wider Golden Mile corridor.

decisions.title: Wellington Region Head Start Proposal
decisions.summary: This report seeks a decision from Council on the submission of a Wellington Region Head Start proposal and outlines the next steps should Council approve the submission of a proposal.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.

Notes that a Head Start Proposal is a high-level outline of a potential future governance structure and that Cabinet will determine whether a proposal is agreed in principle and progresses to a detailed design phase. If a Proposal is agreed in principle; there would be a detailed design phase in which all elements of the model; including representation; as well as delivery; would be further developed; subject to the enactment of enabling legislation.
Agrees to submit a proposal to the Head Start process.
Approves the Head Start Proposal (Attachment 1) for submission to the Government; with the following key elements:
A model with:

A single regional unitary authority; with an elected mayor based around catchment boundaries; with the detailed design phase to determine the most appropriate sub-regional governance arrangements which could include at least five community councils;

Should the final composition of participating councils result in a governance area where arrangements to balance rural and urban representation are not required; exploration of an alternative unitary authority representation model with a greater number of wards across the region; with the detailed design phase to determine the most appropriate sub-regional governance arrangements.
Māori wards included within the unitary authority structure and any sub regional structure to provide for Māori electoral representation; including matawaka;

Mana whenua partnership arrangements established at governance level to recognise iwi as Treaty partners. The form of those arrangements to be co-designed with iwi during the detailed design phase; on the basis that provision for Māori wards alone does not honour Te Tiriti o Waitangi or treaty settlement obligations;
A referendum prior to the detailed design being submitted to Cabinet for decision in March 2027.

An implementation programme that provides for establishment by the 2028 Local Government elections through enabling legislation; reducing compliance requirements and support for transition including an establishment committee and transition board.

For the proposal to also strongly highlight the request to Government for additional financial assistance to support transition and implementation costs; including consideration of arrangements similar to those provided to support the establishment of Auckland Council.

or the proposal to include a request to Government to confirm alongside its September 2026 decision whether it will introduce legislation; or by any other instrument; stop or delay the review of the Long-Term Plan due 30 June 2027; noting that were it to do so LTP amendments may be required in some instances.
Authorises the Mayor to:
Agree and sign the finalised Head Start Proposal;

Agree any amendments to the Head Start Proposal necessary to reflect the decisions of other local authorities; within the mandate provided by Council at this meeting; including the inclusion of statements reflecting the views of each local authority covered by the Proposal;
Agrees that the final Head Start Proposal; including any amendments made under delegated authority; be reported to elected members and Pou Māori/Iwi representatives prior to submission to Government.
Authorises the Chair of the Mayoral Forum to submit the Head Start Proposal to Government on behalf of the councils who have agreed to it by 9 August 2026.

Notes that Cabinet has indicated that it will make a decision on Head Start proposals before the General Election in November 2026 and that if a proposal is accepted; Government may seek modifications to the proposal.

Agrees that further work be undertaken by officers ahead of the Cabinet decision to advance planning for the detailed design phase; including programme planning and engagement with the market for future procurement.
recommendations.actionComment: Cabinet has postponed their decision until early 2027. Officers are awaiting the outcome of the General Election and any direction provided by the new Government.

recommendations.text: Direct the Chief Executive; if a Wellington proposal is progressed to the detailed design phase; to work collaboratively with those councils supporting the Head Start proposal; report back in early October 2026 with recommendations for a programme of work to develop detailed design; including details of governance arrangements; a Wellington City Council reference group made up of Representatives; resources; funding; mana whenua participation and reporting arrangements as well as options for community engagement and communications such as a poll of electors or referendum
recommendations.actionComment: Cabinet has postponed their decision until early 2027. Officers are awaiting the outcome of the General Election and any direction provided by the new Government.

recommendations.text: Agrees that further discussions be held with any Councils that do not support the Head Start Proposal to explore whether they wish to continue to work collaboratively on a regional basis.

Agrees that; following a Cabinet decision scheduled for September 2026; elected members will be briefed on matters to be addressed through the detailed design phase and that advice will be brought to Council for a decision on Council’s initial position; which will include; but not be limited to

Retaining opportunities for community perspectives to inform regional decision making; including through advisory bodies or similar mechanisms that recognise the value of existing community advisory arrangements;

Prioritising the design of environmental regulation functions; recognising that the disestablishment of regional councils will require clear and effective arrangements for the delivery of these functions; and
options analysis for sub-regional governance arrangements; including representation; voting systems; delegations; powers; decision-making responsibilities; funding and governance relationships.
Notes:
The importance of the detailed design phase considering representation arrangements that provide for equity of representation and appropriately reflect population distribution across the region.

That Wellington City Council agrees with amendments raised by Porirua City Council that support the principle of fair and proportional representation in relation to population for both the unitary authority; community councils and/or any other model of sub-regional governance.
Agrees to approve the following position statement reflecting the views of the Wellington City Council for inclusion in the Head Start Proposal submitted to the Government:

Wellington City Council supports progressing a Head Start proposal for the Wellington region and working collaboratively with mana whenua; communities; other councils and the Government through any detailed design phase. Initial community engagement undertaken across the region and in Wellington city identified greater support for a metropolitan unitary authority model alongside a Wairarapa unitary authority. We note that South Wairarapa District Council has voted to support joining a single regional unitary authority. From information provided to mayors and councils; we have to reconcile the significant climate resilience; infrastructure and environmental challenges facing the wider region and acknowledge that; when assessed against the Government's Head Start criteria; there is both a case for a single regional unitary authority or two regional unitary authorities that can support integrated planning; service delivery and long-term financial sustainability across the Wellington and Wairarapa region. We recognise that potential regional and sub-regional governance arrangements were developed within the timeframes available for preparation of a high-level Head Start proposal and that further work will be required during the detailed design phase to determine the most appropriate representation; governance and decision-making arrangements. Those arrangements acknowledge different parts of the region have a different nature and character to others. Now that there is greater certainty regarding participation in the Head Start process; the detailed design phase will provide the opportunity to fully assess and develop regional and sub-regional governance arrangements; including how local communities are represented and engaged in future decision-making. We seek a detailed design phase that further develops representation arrangements; mana whenua partnership arrangements; and a programme of community engagement and consultation; including a referendum before a final proposal is submitted to Cabinet.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.

recommendations.text: Receive the information
Note that the 2026/27 Annual Plan has been prepared based on the decisions and recommendations of the Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee meeting of 27 May 2025.

Note following the decisions made; the budget has been updated and results in an average rate increase on a like-for-like basis excluding water rates; of 5.9 percent after growth (including the sludge levy).

Note that while the Council is forecasting a surplus of $42.4m for 2026/27; the balanced budget benchmark required under the Local Government (Financial Reporting and Prudence) Regulations 2014 is not met at 98%. This is due to capital revenue; ring fenced activities; not funding a portion of the depreciation expense; and the debt funding of some operating expenditure.

Agree that having regard to the requirements of section 100 of the Local Government Act 2002; the Council’s significant forecasting assumptions and the Revenue and Financing Policy; it is financially prudent not to set a level of operating revenue that meets the projected operating expenses of Council.

Note that Council has debt funded limited operating expenditure; which is inconsistent with the Council’s Revenue and Financing Policy but is included in the 2026/27 Annual Plan to manage intergenerational equity.

Note that the closing forecast net borrowings at 30 June 2027 is $1.5b and a debt to revenue ratio of 211 percent which exceeds the self-imposed limit of 200 percent per the Councils’ financial strategy in the 2024-34 Long-Term Plan.
Agree to Attachments 1 to 3 and note that the 2026/27 Annual Plan will be presented at the Council meeting on 25 June 2026.

Note that all key performance indicators (KPIs) for water activities (stormwater; wastewater; and drinking water) have been removed from the Annual Plan; as responsibility for monitoring these KPIs now sits with the new water entity; Tiaki Wai.
Recommend that Te Kaunihera o Pōneke | Council:
Adopt the 2026/27 Annual Plan (Attachment 1 to 3); and
Delegate to the Chief Executive and the Mayor the authority to make any minor editorial changes that may arise as part of the publication process.

recommendations.text: Note the findings of the CCO Operating Model Review undertaken by MartinJenkins; including that financial sustainability is the primary system level challenge across Council’s CCOs; with Wellington Zoo representing the most significant and immediate financial sustainability challenge.
Agree to elements of the recommended Phase 1 pathway consistent with the framework recommended by MartinJenkins; which retains the current CCO structure (enhanced status quo); including:
exploring a stronger coordinating role for WellingtonNZ to support cross‑CCO collaboration on marketing; audience development; insights and product development.

Note officers have explored the option of transitioning Capital E back into Council from Wheako Pōneke Experience Wellington and consider that it is unlikely to deliver operational efficiencies and may increase costs; so are not recommending it at this time

Agree that broader Phase 2 CCO amalgamation options identified by MartinJenkins are not progressed at this time.

Note that Wellington Zoo represents the most significant and immediate financial sustainability challenge across Council’s CCO portfolio; including forecast operating deficits from FY27 and a potential going-concern risk; and that options to improve the Zoo’s financial sustainability are being developed for Councillor consideration through the 2027–37 Long-Term Plan.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.
Agree to “Option 3” - adopt a maximum vehicle cap of up to 2;000 devices with authority delegated to officers to implement and manage vehicle allocations to operators on a staged basis.
Agree to increase the Code of Practice from a minimum 25% deployment in suburban areas to mitigate disproportionate impacts in dense urban areas of increased vehicles.
Agree that if Committee agrees to increase the device cap; officers will then negotiate increases to per trip fees and that device increase is dependent on these negotiations being successful.
Agree further options for dedicated micromobility parking spaces will be investigated and approval sought through a Traffic Resolution process
Agree that within the vehicle cap each operator has discretion for which types of micromobility devices they offer including e-scooters; seated e-scooters and e-bikes.

Direct officers to report back on safety options in shared spaces within the inner city; to reduce the potential for harm between pedestrians and other modes of transport such as E scooters and cycles.

finalClauses.text: Receive the information.

Agree to increase the Code of Practice from a minimum 25% deployment in suburban areas to mitigate disproportionate impacts in dense urban areas of increased vehicles.
Agree that if Committee agrees to increase the device cap; officers will then negotiate increases to per trip fees and that device increase is dependent on these negotiations being successful.

Recommend that Te Kaunihera o Pōneke | Council:

Agree not to continue with the current 2021-approved scope for the Golden Mile project (with a $139.4 million transport budget; co-funded 49% by Council and 51% by NZTA); while retaining only $1.5 million of Council funding in FY2026/27 for make-safe works as part of the WP1 Kent/ Cambridge outcomes and removing remaining budget.

Direct officers to bring back to the Te Hoe Matua | City Strategy and Delivery Committee by June 2027 a Detailed Business Case; which is informed by existing planning and design work; for targeted Golden Mile transport corridor improvements and Courtenay Place urban regeneration; within a reduced Council net investment range capped at $20-$40 million and seeking to optimise cost recovery through NZTA co-funding of the transport benefits. This option would:

Retain existing unspent Long-term Plan budget provision of $20 - $40 million net capital expenditure to preserve the ability to progress a future corridor intervention through the Detailed Business Case.
Agree budget provision of $1.5 million capital expenditure in FY26/27 for make-safe works and $2 million to develop the Detailed Business Case
Agree budget provision of $1.5 million capital expenditure in FY26/27 for make-safe works and $2 million to develop the Detailed Business Case.

Note that officers will optimise the development of the detailed business case to enable full development of the preferred option; in a way that incorporates early contractor involvement so that momentum is retained for construction

Note that; in line with Council’s Investment Decision Making Framework; Committee approval will be sought for: a Project Brief; which will confirm objectives and the benefits sought and the investment appetite; the high level options that will be developed further in the business case; and any constraints (including affordability) or parameters that the project should needs to work within; and the Detailed Business Case which will enable an investment decision on the preferred option.

Note officers will bring back advice to the Te Hoe Matua | City Strategy and Delivery Committee on the existing approved traffic resolutions for the Golden Mile project once Council has determined the project’s direction.
Direct officers to report back on establishing any related project board including how elected members will be appropriately represented

Requests officers to report back to the Te Hoe Matua | City Strategy and Delivery Committee by September 2026 with options for establishing a Precinct Accelerator Fund; to further support co-investment initiatives to improve the public realm in the medium term.

Delegates authority to the Chief Executive to determine how to fund an additional $91;000 per annum budget that is required to increase cleaning along Courtenay Place from monthly to weekly but not currently funded in the Annual Plan 2026/2027.

recommendations.text: approves entry into the Transfer Agreement (Attachment 1) with Tiaki Wai; noting that the terms and conditions of the Transfer Agreement have been developed with input from across all Shareholding Councils; the Tiaki Wai Establishment Team and legal representatives involved in the process; and that the Tiaki Wai Board will be meeting to approve the Transfer Agreement on 11 June 2026;
approves the transfer of debt from the Council to Tiaki Wai; as provided for (and subject; where applicable; to the post completion adjustments contemplated by) the Transfer Agreement;

approves the transfer of statutory responsibilities; land and interests in land; assets; contracts; approvals and all other matters from the Council to Tiaki Wai; subject to finalising the relevant Transfer Schedules that will be appended to the Transfer Agreement; resolution of any associated processes under the Transfer Agreement; and completion of all necessary processes and statutory requirements; and for that purpose:
delegates to the Mayor and Chief Executive the power to finalise the Transfer Schedules; and
directs Council officers to report back when all processes and requirements have been completed.
notes that not all land on which water services assets or infrastructure is located will transfer to Tiaki Wai; and as a consequence:

notes the Delegations Policy applies and authorises officers with relevant delegated authority to enter into any leases; licences to occupy and easements over Council land considered necessary to ensure appropriate rights to Tiaki Wai and the Council; where land does not transfer.

until such time as formal access arrangements have been secured by way of other appropriate instruments; approves the grant of a standing licence in favour of Tiaki Wai in the form attached to the Transfer Agreement as Schedule 1; and

notes that there are a large number of water services assets or infrastructure located on private land with easements to Council; and these easements will not transfer immediately to Tiaki Wai until Council is satisfied that each easement is legally able to be transferred. Until that process is completed; Tiaki Wai has the power under the Local Government (Water Services) Act to enter private land for purposes connected with water services.

approves the entering into services agreements with Tiaki Wai; which addresses various shared and transitional services that will be provided between the Council and Tiaki Wai to ensure continuity of waters service delivery and other ancillary matters from 1 July 2026; and delegates to the Chief Executive of Wellington City Council the power to negotiate and agree the terms of the various shared and transitional services and execute those agreements on Council’s behalf;

approves the Council entering into all associated agreements; deeds; notices; side letters and other documents contemplated by; or required in connection with the Transfer Agreement; with the approval and execution of those documents delegated to Chief Executive and other Officers in accordance with the Delegations Policy.

delegates to Tiaki Wai the power to administer and enforce Wellington City Council Water Services Bylaw 2024 and the Wellington Trade Waste Bylaw 2016 as per the attached Instrument of Delegation (Attachment 4);

approves the making of an invitation to Tiaki Wai to undertake; for all Shareholding Councils; an initial review of all existing water services bylaws that apply across the Service Area; and to then report back to the Partners Committee by no later than 30 April 2027 with recommendations on whether new or amended bylaws should be made by the four territorial authority Shareholding Councils;
delegates to the Mayor and Chief Executive to:
agree the Transfer Agreement on behalf of the Council subject to providing elected members a reasonable opportunity before signing to review the final transfer agreement and schedules;
execute the Transfer Agreement (which can be done by the Mayor or Chief Executive acting alone)
publish the final executed version of the Transfer Agreement on the Council’s website (with any appropriate or required redactions); no later than 7 July 2026;
do such other things in connection with the Transfer Agreement; as they may consider necessary.
Direct officers to provide six-monthly report backs to elected members for the duration of the two year wash up period.
Note that Council has serious concerns around the transfer of WCC owned water assets that have not yet been adequately addressed ahead of a 1 July 2026 Transfer.
Agree for the Mayor to advocate for the Commerce Commission to have stronger price regulation powers in relation to Tiaki Wai.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.
Recommend that Te Kaunihera o Pōneke | Council:

approves entry into the Transfer Agreement (Attachment 1) with Tiaki Wai; noting that the terms and conditions of the Transfer Agreement have been developed with input from across all Shareholding Councils; the Tiaki Wai Establishment Team and legal representatives involved in the process; and that the Tiaki Wai Board will be meeting to approve the Transfer Agreement on 11 June 2026;
approves the transfer of debt from the Council to Tiaki Wai; as provided for (and subject; where applicable; to the post completion adjustments contemplated by) the Transfer Agreement;

approves the transfer of statutory responsibilities; land and interests in land; assets; contracts; approvals and all other matters from the Council to Tiaki Wai; subject to finalising the relevant Transfer Schedules that will be appended to the Transfer Agreement; resolution of any associated processes under the Transfer Agreement; and completion of all necessary processes and statutory requirements; and for that purpose:
delegates to the Mayor and Chief Executive the power to finalise the Transfer Schedules; and
directs Council officers to report back when all processes and requirements have been completed.
notes that not all land on which water services assets or infrastructure is located will transfer to Tiaki Wai; and as a consequence:

notes the Delegations Policy applies and authorises officers with relevant delegated authority to enter into any leases; licences to occupy and easements over Council land considered necessary to ensure appropriate rights to Tiaki Wai and the Council; where land does not transfer.

until such time as formal access arrangements have been secured by way of other appropriate instruments; approves the grant of a standing licence in favour of Tiaki Wai in the form attached to the Transfer Agreement as Schedule 1; and

notes that there are a large number of water services assets or infrastructure located on private land with easements to Council; and these easements will not transfer immediately to Tiaki Wai until Council is satisfied that each easement is legally able to be transferred. Until that process is completed; Tiaki Wai has the power under the Local Government (Water Services) Act to enter private land for purposes connected with water services.

approves the entering into services agreements with Tiaki Wai; which addresses various shared and transitional services that will be provided between the Council and Tiaki Wai to ensure continuity of waters service delivery and other ancillary matters from 1 July 2026; and delegates to the Chief Executive of Wellington City Council the power to negotiate and agree the terms of the various shared and transitional services and execute those agreements on Council’s behalf;

approves the Council entering into all associated agreements; deeds; notices; side letters and other documents contemplated by; or required in connection with the Transfer Agreement; with the approval and execution of those documents delegated to Chief Executive and other Officers in accordance with the Delegations Policy.

delegates to Tiaki Wai the power to administer and enforce Wellington City Council Water Services Bylaw 2024 and the Wellington Trade Waste Bylaw 2016 as per the attached Instrument of Delegation (Attachment 4);

approves the making of an invitation to Tiaki Wai to undertake; for all Shareholding Councils; an initial review of all existing water services bylaws that apply across the Service Area; and to then report back to the Partners Committee by no later than 30 April 2027 with recommendations on whether new or amended bylaws should be made by the four territorial authority Shareholding Councils;
delegates to the Mayor and Chief Executive to:
agree the Transfer Agreement on behalf of the Council subject to providing elected members a reasonable opportunity before signing to review the final transfer agreement and schedules;
execute the Transfer Agreement (which can be done by the Mayor or Chief Executive acting alone)
publish the final executed version of the Transfer Agreement on the Council’s website (with any appropriate or required redactions); no later than 7 July 2026;
do such other things in connection with the Transfer Agreement; as they may consider necessary.
Direct officers to provide six-monthly report backs to elected members for the duration of the two year wash up period.
Agree for the Mayor to advocate for the Commerce Commission to have stronger price regulation powers in relation to Tiaki Wai.

amendments.text: Defer the establishment of Tiaki Wai Metro Water and associated transfer arrangements until 1 March 2027 to allow for completion of remediation of Moa Point; a better understanding of proposed amalgamation; the inclusion of commerce commission oversight and powers on pricing to ensure future increases are justifiable and affordable for Wellingtonians and to allow the outstanding items to be resolved so we clearly understand our future liability

Note that this would be significantly inconsistent with the Long-term Plan and associated plans and strategies because the Long-term plan provides for Wellington City Council to cease delivery of Water Services from 1 July 2026.
Note that Council intends to amend the Long-term Plan to accommodate the decision in 2.1.
Note that Council has serious concerns around the transfer of WCC owned water assets that have not yet been adequately addressed ahead of a 1 July 2026 Transfer.
