decisions.title: Quarterly 3 Performance Report
decisions.summary: This report to Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee provides performance information for Quarter three of Year Two (2025/26) of the 2024-34 LongTerm plan (LTP). The information in the quarterly report supports governance oversight and service delivery performance monitoring of: • Budget performance; • Strategic activity area performance e.g. delivery of key service performance indicators; and • Key strategies and their action plans. This report also outlines requirements for budget changes for the current financial year; to ensure spend aligns with Officer’s delegated authority.

recommendations.text: Receive the Quarter three (Q3) Performance Report on the 2024-34 Long-term Plan (LTP).
Note

Officers are continuing to undertake work required from the February storm and April flooding events. Expenses are being funded from other savings where possible but are likely to require additional funding; officers will look to bring this back to Council for approval in future if required.
Decisions about capital carry forwards and bring forwards for 2025/26 will be considered by the Committee through the 2026/27 Annual Plan deliberations.
Recommend that Te Kaunihera o Pōneke | Council agrees:
To increase the operating expenditure budget for Wellington Zoo (2.6.1 Conservation Visitor Attractions) by $0.75m in FY 2025/26 to fund the forecast operating deficit.
To transfer $1.4m from the HUP2 capital expenditure budget (5.2.4 Housing) to the operating expenditure budget as debt funded opex (5.2.4 Housing); to fund rehousing costs.

To reduce the debt funded operating expenditure budget by $7.275m for the City to Sea Bridge (6.1.2 Public Spaces and Centres Development) and increase the capital expenditure budget by $1m for the City to Sea Bridge and Capital E project (10.1.1 Organisational Projects).
To increase the capital revenue and capital expenditure budgets for waste renewals (2.2.1 Waste Minimisation) by $0.031m for 2025/26 to replace a compost screen on a truck.
To decrease the capital expenditure budget for carbon credit purchase (2.2.1 Waste Minimisation) by $4.226m for 2025/26 due to the liability being funded by existing credits.

To increase the operating expenditure budget for Wellington Water for the Moa Point incident (2.4.2 Sewage Treatment) by the value of the unexpected events reserve of $2.952m for 2025/26. This is to be funded from the balance sheet; there will be no debt impact.

decisions.title: Deliberation of the 2026-27 Annual Plan
decisions.summary: This report provides Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee (the Committee) with submissions on Council’s draft 2026/27 Annual Plan Consultation Document; an analysis of submitter views on the key consultation issues as outlined in the Consultation Document and an opportunity to determine whether any changes are required before the 2026/27 annual plan is recommended to Council for adoption on 25 June 2026. This report also provides advice on the sale of the Council’s holding of NZU’s and makes a recommendation for the sale of a portion of these; and the policy on the management of carbon credits going forward. These Committee deliberations are the final decision stage for developing the 2026/27 Annual Plan; and the decisions from this paper will be recommended to Te Kaunihera o Pōneke | Council on 25 June 2026.
reciprocalReports: Adoption of the 2026-27 Annual Plan

recommendations.text: Receive the information.

Note that the decision outlined in this paper will be developed into the final 2026/27 Annual Plan and the rates setting paper for adoption by Council on 25 June 2026. Any changes that occur after these committee deliberations other than editorial changes will mean that the Council is not in a position to adopt the Annual Plan by 30 June 2026 and set the rates for 2026/27.
Receive the submissions (available online as ‘other documents’ on this meeting agenda).
Note the consultation process; engagement tools and consultation and survey results for the 2026/27 Annual Plan consultation and receive the community feedback as outlined in Attachment 1.
Note that the 2026/27 Consultation Budget included a forecast average rates increase on a like-for-like basis excluding water rates; of 7.4 percent including the sludge minimisation levy.

Note that the impact of savings identified during the consultation period; proposed carry forwards; and cost pressures have been reflected in the updated 2026/27 Annual Plan budget and result in an updated forecast average rates increase of 5.8 percent including the sludge minimisation levy.
Agree the following key proposals:

Key proposal 1: Short-term accommodation - Introduce a new general rates differential for short-term accommodation providers; set at 2.6 times the base general rate (with the changes noted in the body of the report);
Key proposal 2: Paneke Pōneke Bike Network - Option A: Reduce cycleways programme for 2026/27 and review (preferred);
Key proposal 3: Contaminated waste fees: Option A - Increase the Contaminated Soil and Special Waste (Asbestos) fee incrementally over the next three years (preferred); and
Key proposal 4: Cremation fees - Option A: Increase cremation fees by 20 percent (preferred).
Fees and user charges: All fees changes including new fees and fees changes above inflation as outlined in Attachment 3

Note interim fees for booking rooms/spaces at Te Matapihi; from its opening in March 2026 to 30 June 2026; have been approved by Council and are currently being charged to the public. New (full) fees to apply from 1 July 2026 are included in Attachment 3.
Agree that $0.43m of the proposed savings identified to be achieved from the Social and Recreation activity areas be achieved as follows:
$0.15m per annum has been identified though small savings across multiple areas without impacting levels of service;
$0.12m in additional revenue in 2026/27 due to the delayed closure of Kilbirnie Rec Centre for upgrade works;
$0.16m in 2026/27 by rephasing the floor sanding at Akau Tangi Sports Centre to 2027/28;
Agree that the remaining $0.22m of savings proposed through the Social and Recreation activity area be:
removed and the impact will increase the average rates increase; or
identify the savings to be achieved within another activity / budget area.
Agree the following ‘other key Annual Plan’ changes consulted on and identified and agreed in the 12 March Committee meeting as follows:
Reduction of $0.50m across the Economic Grants. These fund WellingtonNZ; Destination Wellington marketing; support major events; and includes the City Growth Fund.
Reduction of $0.26m in Heritage Resilience and Regeneration Fund through removing funding for earthquake prone building works due to government changes in this area.
Investigating establishing an Urban Development Office to make efficiency savings of $1.00m and streamline services for the public.

$0.50m saving in support for community Climate mitigation activities and transport education initiatives; focusing instead on Climate adaptation; and mitigation activities that deliver demonstrable emission reductions.
$0.76m reduction in the budget for activities in the re-opened Te Ngākau Civic Square
$15.90m in targeted internal savings including:
not funding $13.50m depreciation
reducing the consultancy budget by $1.10m
making changes to our Communications; Engagement; International Relations; and Property services to make efficiencies where possible; and
a reduction $70k in international tourism attraction funding for WellingtonNZ.
Agree that unfunded depreciation with be made up as follows:
$0.20m in trails depreciation;
$4.60m in structures depreciation (25 percent of total structures depreciation);
$8.70m in increased unfunded transport depreciation.

Agree to a phased reduction of the Ōtari Wilton Bush Laboratory over the 2026/27; including retention of one FTE and engagement with stakeholders and iwi on future options. Savings of $0.11m opex from baseline in 2026/27; and total saving of $0.21m from 2027/28.
Agree capital rephasing as outlined in the 12 March Committee report including:
Ian Galloway Park
Frank Kitts Park
Grenada North Sports Hub and Synthetic Turf
Lincolnshire/ Stebbings
Mark Ave to Grenada North
Harbour Quays
Recreation Centre Renewals
Evans Bay Marina

Note that as part of the quarter three forecasting process officers have reviewed the 2025/26 capital programme and identified a number of projects that will not be completed or fully spent during 2025/26 and will now be completed in 2026/27 or later.

. Agree the following carry forwards and rephasing from 2025/26 to 2026/27 and beyond as detailed in Attachment 2 and outlined below; with final amounts to be adjusted as necessary to reflect any project carry forwards not being approved:
$182.40m recommended to be carried forward from 2025/26 to:
$2.90m recommended to be brought forward and rephased from 2026/27 to 2025/26;
$4.50m recommended to be rephased from 2026/27 to out years.
Agree to transfer budget between projects (included in the above totals):
Rephase $1.20m from the 2025/26 budget from the Te Ngakau Loading Dock project to the 2026/27 budget for the City to Sea Bridge and Capital E project;
Rephase $1.10m from the 2025/26 Bridge Renewals budget to the 2026/27 Retaining Walls Renewals budget.

Note that the recommended carry forwards and updated depreciation assumptions result in a reduction in the 2026/27 Annual Plan depreciation budget of $6.40m and interest budget of $1.30m compared to the Consutlation Budget and these savings are reflected in the proposed budget
Note that officers have identified operational budgets where it would be financially prudent to rephase expenditure from 2025/26 to 2026/27; as these can be funded without impacting rates.
Agree to the following 2026/27 Annual Plan budget changes which will have no impact on rates:
to rephase $0.90m from 2025/26 to 2026/27 relating to the Waikoukou staff accommodation relocation project funding it from the rates collected in 2025/26;
to rephase $1.90m funding relating to the Karori Events Centre from 2025/26 to 2026/27 and continue to debt fund this amount;
to rephase $0.30m of funding relating to the Payroll Replacement project from 2025/26 to 2026/27 and continue to debt fund this amount;
to rephase $0.50m in operational expenditure from 2025/26 to 2026/27 relating to the Suburban Centre Upgrades programme and funding it from the rates collected in 2025/26.
Agree to include the following contingencies in the 2026/27 Annual Plan;
$0.28m in direct fuel costs applied directly to fuel budgets;
$1.00m fuel related contract contingency to be accessed as required;
$0.20m in Local Government reform costs.

Note that the budget has been updated to reflect a dividend from Wellington International Airport Limited (WIAL) of $18.60m based on advice from WIAL. The consultation budget included a dividend of $19.30m.
Agree to include $5.40m in debt funded opex in both 2026/27 and 2027/28 ($10.8m for the two years) to fund the bypass upgrade as part of the Moa Point wastewater treatment plant remediation.

Note that officers have reviewed the Council’s holding of New Zealand Units under the New Zealand Emissions Trading Scheme and identified that 400;000 units of the Councils total 502;524 holding could be sold over the course of 2026/27 financial year at a minimum price of $50 per unit. The proceeds will be ring fenced to fund existing initiatives under Te Atakura.
Agree to sell 400;000 NZU’s during the 2026/27 financial year with the following conditions:
A minimum price of $50 per unit;
Proceeds will be ringfenced to fund existing planned initiatives under Te Atakura;
Officers will report back on appropriate initiatives during 2026/27 and seek approval for these to funded through sale proceeds.
Agree the Carbon Credit Policy at Attachment 4.

Agree the following ‘other key Annual Plan’ changes consulted on and identified and agreed in the 12 March Committee meeting as follows:
Reduction of $0.50m across the Economic Grants. These fund WellingtonNZ; Destination Wellington marketing; support major events; and includes the City Growth Fund.
Reduction of $0.26m in Heritage Resilience and Regeneration Fund through removing funding for earthquake prone building works due to government changes in this area.
Investigating establishing an Urban Development Office to make efficiency savings of $1.00m and streamline services for the public.

$0.50m saving in support for community Climate mitigation activities and transport education initiatives; focusing instead on Climate adaptation; and mitigation activities that deliver demonstrable emission reductions.
$0.76m reduction in the budget for activities in the re-opened Te Ngākau Civic Square
$15.90m in targeted internal savings including:
not funding $13.50m depreciation
reducing the consultancy budget by $1.10m
making changes to our Communications; Engagement; International Relations; and Property services to make efficiencies where possible; and
a reduction $70k in international tourism attraction funding for WellingtonNZ.
Agree that unfunded depreciation with be made up as follows:
$0.20m in trails depreciation;
$4.60m in structures depreciation (25 percent of total structures depreciation);
$8.70m in increased unfunded transport depreciation.

Agree to a phased reduction of the Ōtari Wilton Bush Laboratory over the 2026/27; including retention of one FTE and engagement with stakeholders and iwi on future options. Savings of $0.11m opex from baseline in 2026/27; and total saving of $0.21m from 2027/28.
Agree capital rephasing as outlined in the 12 March Committee report including:
Ian Galloway Park
Frank Kitts Park
Grenada North Sports Hub and Synthetic Turf
Lincolnshire/ Stebbings
Mark Ave to Grenada North
Harbour Quays
Recreation Centre Renewals
Evans Bay Marina

Note that as part of the quarter three forecasting process officers have reviewed the 2025/26 capital programme and identified a number of projects that will not be completed or fully spent during 2025/26 and will now be completed in 2026/27 or later.

. Agree the following carry forwards and rephasing from 2025/26 to 2026/27 and beyond as detailed in Attachment 2 and outlined below; with final amounts to be adjusted as necessary to reflect any project carry forwards not being approved:
$182.40m recommended to be carried forward from 2025/26 to:
$2.90m recommended to be brought forward and rephased from 2026/27 to 2025/26;
$4.50m recommended to be rephased from 2026/27 to out years.
Agree to transfer budget between projects (included in the above totals):
Rephase $1.20m from the 2025/26 budget from the Te Ngakau Loading Dock project to the 2026/27 budget for the City to Sea Bridge and Capital E project;
Rephase $1.10m from the 2025/26 Bridge Renewals budget to the 2026/27 Retaining Walls Renewals budget.

Note that the recommended carry forwards and updated depreciation assumptions result in a reduction in the 2026/27 Annual Plan depreciation budget of $6.40m and interest budget of $1.30m compared to the Consutlation Budget and these savings are reflected in the proposed budget
Note that officers have identified operational budgets where it would be financially prudent to rephase expenditure from 2025/26 to 2026/27; as these can be funded without impacting rates.
Agree to the following 2026/27 Annual Plan budget changes which will have no impact on rates:
to rephase $0.90m from 2025/26 to 2026/27 relating to the Waikoukou staff accommodation relocation project funding it from the rates collected in 2025/26;

to rephase $1.90m funding relating to the Karori Events Centre from 2025/26 to 2026/27 to enable a decision to be referred to Council in accordance with the resolutions agreed at the Kōrau Tōtōpū | Long Term Plan; Finance; and Performance Committee 22 May 2025
to rephase $0.30m of funding relating to the Payroll Replacement project from 2025/26 to 2026/27 and continue to debt fund this amount;
to rephase $0.50m in operational expenditure from 2025/26 to 2026/27 relating to the Suburban Centre Upgrades programme and funding it from the rates collected in 2025/26.
Agree to include the following contingencies in the 2026/27 Annual Plan;
$0.28m in direct fuel costs applied directly to fuel budgets;
$1.00m fuel related contract contingency to be accessed as required;
$0.20m in Local Government reform costs.

Note that the budget has been updated to reflect a dividend from Wellington International Airport Limited (WIAL) of $18.60m based on advice from WIAL. The consultation budget included a dividend of $19.30m.
Agree to include $5.40m in debt funded opex in both 2026/27 and 2027/28 ($10.8m for the two years) to fund the bypass upgrade as part of the Moa Point wastewater treatment plant remediation.

Note that officers have reviewed the Council’s holding of New Zealand Units under the New Zealand Emissions Trading Scheme and identified that 400;000 units of the Councils total 502;524 holding could be sold over the course of 2026/27 financial year at a minimum price of $50 per unit. The proceeds will be ring fenced to fund existing initiatives under Te Atakura.
Agree to sell 400;000 NZU’s during the 2026/27 financial year with the following conditions:
A minimum price of $50 per unit;
Proceeds will be ringfenced to fund existing planned initiatives under Te Atakura;
Officers will report back on appropriate initiatives during 2026/27 and seek approval for these to funded through sale proceeds.
Agree the Carbon Credit Policy at Attachment 4.

decisions.summary: To seek Council approval to provide targeted; time bound grants to support business viability of a small number of severely impacted businesses in response to the disruption associated with the critical failure of the Moa Point Wastewater Treatment Plant in February 2026.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.
Agree to provide a maximum of $150;000 business relief grants from the City Growth Fund.
Agree the proposed eligibility criteria; and allocation methodology as detailed in this paper

Agree that the grant is to be used only for the purposes outlined in this paper and delegate authority to the Chief Economic and Engagement Officer to finalise and execute grant agreements and release funding in accordance with those agreements.
Direct officers to review and report back by 31 August 2026 on the impacts and delivery of the Moa Point Business Support Grant.

finalClauses.text: Receive the information.
Agree to provide a maximum of $200;000 comprised of $150;000 in business relief grants from the City Growth Fund and $50;000 from organisational savings.

Agree that the grant is to be used only for the purposes outlined in this paper and delegate authority to the Chief Economic and Engagement Officer to finalise and execute grant agreements and release funding in accordance with those agreements.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.
Recommend that Te Kaunihera o Pōneke | Council adopt the 2026/27 Annual Plan Consultation Document (Attachment 1) and the submission form (Attachment 2).
Recommend that Te Kaunihera o Pōneke | Council adopt the supporting information for the consultation on the 2026/27 Annual Plan (presented on the meeting day) comprising the following:
Annual Plan Prospective Financial Statements
Annual Plan Funding Impact Statements
Annual Plan Rating Funding Impact Statements
Proposed 2026/27 Annual Plan changes to user fees and charges (Attachment 3).

Recommend that Te Kaunihera o Pōneke | Council delegate the Mayor and the Chief Executive to make minor editorial changes; and updates to the Consultation Document and supporting information to reflect committee decision-making and as part of finalising the material for public consultation.

a proposed rates increase; on a like-for-like basis; excluding water rates; of 7.4% (after growth) and inclusive of the Sludge Minimisation Levy; compared to the 12.7% forecast in the LTP;

a forecast closing net debt of $1.7b compared to the $1.6b forecast in the LTP. A proposed debt to revenue ratio of 212% which exceeds Councils self-imposed limit of 200%; compared to the 198% forecast in the LTP; and
a forecast net deficit of $2.3m (excluding any fair value movements).

Note the further revised KPI target for Experience Wellington (Wellington Museums Trust) for student and education visits; which has changed from 17;445 to 13;980 since the revised target was presented to the Committee on 12 March 2026.

decisions.summary: This report seeks agreement on the design of the Disaster Resilience Fund (DRF) and the plan for its implementation and establishment. Options relating to the key design decisions are presented in this report. The documents that set up the DRF will be brought back to Committee for approval in May/June 2026.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.
Recommend that Te Kaunihera o Pōneke | Council:
Agree to set up the DRF as an “Internal fund” ring-fenced on the balance sheet of the Council.
recommendations.actionComment: Governance documents to be approved in November 2026

recommendations.text: Agree to the establishment of a DRF Committee consisting of three independent members (including Chair and deputy); two elected members (including the Mayor); and mana whenua representation.
recommendations.actionComment: Governance documents to be approved in November 2026 noting impact from Systems Improvement Bill on the removal of voting rights for unelected members

recommendations.text: Agree that the DRF Committee will report to Council twice yearly (at the end of quarter two and quarter four) on the performance of the DRF.

recommendations.text: Agree that access to the DRF is by special distribution based on criteria outlined in the report. The Council would request access to the DRF; and the DRF Committee would make a recommendation to Council about the amount to be withdrawn.
recommendations.actionComment: Governance documents to be approved in November 2026

recommendations.text: Agree that the Council has the flexibility to use the funds as required once a special distribution has been approved.
recommendations.actionComment: Governance documents to be approved in November 2026

recommendations.text: Agree to an ordinary distribution from the DRF that matches forgone revenue from the ground leases for 2026/27.

Agree that the DRF will be listed as a Strategic Asset of the Council under the Council’s Significance and Engagement Policy.

recommendations.text: Agree that the DRF Committee will endure over triennia.
recommendations.actionComment: Governance documents to be approved in November 2026

recommendations.text: Agree to allow for additional sources of capitalisation of the DRF by resolution.
recommendations.actionComment: Governance documents to be approved in November 2026

decisions.title: 2026-27 Annual Plan Draft Budget
decisions.summary: This report to Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee (the Committee) seeks agreement on the following key matters: a. the 2026/27 Annual Plan draft budget; and b. the proposed changes to Fees & Charges for 2026/27. The Committee’s decisions will be used to develop the 2026/27 Annual Plan Consultation Document; which will be presented to Committee for adoption on 26 March 2026.
reciprocalReports: Adoption of the 2026-27 Annual Plan Consultation Document
Adoption of the 2026-27 Annual Plan

recommendations.text: Receive the information.
2026/27 Annual Plan budget: Note that the 2026/27 Annual Plan draft budget in this report for consideration by Committee is based on:
Year three of the amended 2024-34 LTP;
Updated for movements in inflation; interest; and depreciation;

Early work by officers to reduce the budget; by absorbing inflationary pressure; applying vacancy management principles; undertaking a line-by-line review of revenue and expenditures; and recognising options not to fully fund depreciation; and
All the recommendations of the Revenue and Financial Value Working Group.
Note that:

The early work by officers (identified above and presented to elected members in December 2025) reduced the planned rates increase from 12.7 percent (as reflected in the amended 2024-34 LTP) down to 9.4 percent;
If the recommendations of the Revenue and Financial Value (R&FV) Working Party are adopted in full the rates increase would reduce to 7.4 percent; and

If the Committee sought to reduce the rates increase below 7.4 percent; it would need to identify and make further decisions on either the funding of depreciation and / or levels of service at this meeting.

Note that there was insufficient time for the Revenue and Financial Value Review Working Group to fully consider and make recommendations on the 2026/27 capital programme prior to referral to this committee. Recommendations and options are therefore presented to this Committee for decision-making.

Note the budget does not reflect the impact from changes to the capital programme regarding depreciation; interest expenses; and labour charges. The budget does factor in growth in the ratepayer base however this will be updated following further analysis up to June 2026.

Note there is considerable uncertainty about the implications of the failure of the Moa Point wastewater treatment plant on 4 February 2026; and in relation to the financing of the additional funding of $71m for the sludge minimisation plant (clauses 39 and 40 regards).
Agree the proposed changes to the capital programme as below; and detailed in Attachment 1:

Part A: Rephasing of capital works budget to better align with work programmes. C1 Ian Galloway Park C2 Frank Kitts Park C3 Grenada North Sports Hub and Synthetic Turf C4 Lincolnshire/ Stebbings C5 Mark Ave to Grenada North C6 Bus Priority Improvements C7 Harbour Quays C8 Recreation Centre Renewals C9 Evans Bay Marina
Part B: options for changes in the capital programme in 2026/27 to generate savings.
C10 Cycleways (including minor works budget (a) Prioritise completion of primary network in CBD (b) Adjust programme by a different amount (c) Retain programme as per existing LTP amendment
Safer Routes to School (a) Remove capital budget for works (and associated revenue) (b) Keep budget or reduce by a different amount
C12 Speed management Upgrades
C13 Carbon purchases (a) No purchase of carbon credits in 2026/27 (b) Keep budget as planned
Part C: Capital works where no change is recommended. C14 Arts installation C15 Parking Renewals C16 Parking Upgrades C17 Footpath Upgrades C18 Green Network Plan
Agree not to fully fund the depreciation:
On Council owned structures up to 25 percent of $4.6m
on transport assets based on NZTA funding of $8.7m.
Agree to debt fund the Archives Digitisation project of $2.7m which has been reclassified as operating expenditure with repayment through rates over ten years.

Agree to rephase the Payroll Replacement project from 2025/26 to 2026/27 and 2027/28; and to debt fund the operating expenditure portion of the project being $6.5m; with repayment through rates over ten years.

Agree to changes in the social housing budgets which result in an overall reduction of approximately $20m for capital expenditure and an increase of $3m for operating expenditure over the period of the 2024-34 LTP (2026/27 – 2033/34):
increase the Housing Upgrade Programme (HUP2) by $61m for Capex and $3m for Opex to reflect GST inclusive figures and rephase the programme for the period of the 2024-34 LTP.
reduce the housing renewals by $81m to reflect integration with the HUP2 programme and cost savings.
Fees and User charges: Agree the 2026/27 proposed changes to Fees and User charges as outlined in the body of the report and Attachment 2.

Agree the interim Te Matapihi fees - applying from 14 March 2026 (when its bookable spaces first become available for public hire) to 30 June 2026 - ahead of the full fee schedule starting from 1 July 2026. These fees are outlined in the body of the report.
Performance measures: Agree the changes to the Key Performance Indicators (Attachment 3):
Wellington Museums Trust: Student and Education visits – change in target.
Number of critical transport structures: b. Road bridge – change in underlying methodology.

Other: Note that Officers will report back on whether to proceed with the organics; waste and collections changes. This will include information on the infrastructure and services planning with associated financial implications.

Agree that the introduction of a new general rates differential (lower than the Commercial; Industrial and Business differential) for short-term accommodation providers will be incorporated into the next rates review with final recommendations to inform the 2027 Long-term Plan.
Note that officers will prepare the Consultation Document based on the decisions of this Committee meeting and bring that back for adoption on 26 March 2026.
Note that officers will prepare the Consultation Document based on the decisions of this Committee meeting and bring that back for adoption on 26 March 2026.

amendments.text: C10 Cycleways (including minor works budget) (b) Adjust programme by a different amount i. Agree to complete the Bunny St ($2.5 million) connection to the waterfront and the Brooklyn upgrade ($4.1 million) to connect the primary network. ii. Agree that the next phase of the bike network programme; including Victoria St; be deferred for prioritisation in 2027 and subject to a rapid review of all approved capital projects valued at $1 million or more where construction has not started (or a future tranche has not started). iii. Agree the next phase of construction will be brought back to a committee for assurance it is realistic and affordable. iv. That City Streets/Renewals Programme be added to “Part B” with the following options for public consultation: (a) Defer the capital budget for the renewal of Te Aro Park; cycleways; and other works (and associated revenue) (b) Continue with the renewal of Te Aro Park but pause the rest of the capital budget for cycleways and other works (and associated revenue) (c) Keep the current budget (d) Defer the capital budget for all cycleway works (and associated revenue) until the 2027 LTP.
Agree to consult on the following additional options to the Revenue and Finance Review Working Group recommendations:
Increase crematorium fees by 5% from 2025/26 (25a in Attachment 2)
Increase contaminated waste fees by 5% from 2025/26 (32 in Attachment 2)
Agree in respect of short-term accommodation providers that the formal position of Council is to support the introduction of a bed tax to recoup usage on infrastructure via Central Government.
Agree to consult on a new general rates differential of 2.6:1 for short-term accommodation providers in the 2026/27 Annual Plan.
Agree to develop an implementation plan for the new general rates differential in the 2026/27 FY.

Agree that post-implementation of a new general rates differential; that officers will report back after 6 months with an overview of the effectiveness of the new general rates differential for short-term accommodation providers including revenue received; compliance rates and property market impacts.

Note the differential will apply to rating units that are used for short-term accommodation. This is defined as the rental; or availability for rental; of entire houses or units on the rating unit that would otherwise be used for residential purposes:
for periods of less than one month and
where that house or unit is; or has been; made available for short-term accommodation for more than 60 days within the financial year.
Note this explicitly excludes granny flats; sleepouts; and dual key homes that are used for non-commercial purposes or are self-contained but do not meet the criteria for short-term accommodation.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.

amendments.text: Approve the attached submission on the Planning Bill 2025 and Natural Environment Bill 2025 with the following changes:
To Part 1: Supported components:
Clause 3. j); add the reduced territorial authority role to protect significant historic heritage only; instead of historic heritage more generally.
To Part 2: Components that need to be changed:

Clause 11. F); add that to avoid the need to provide regulatory relief; matters of heritage in a local area can be determined solely by council and removed if desired. Council are able to exercise reasonable discretion in matters of economic; cultural; urban and other outcomes in whether a heritage listing is appropriate.

After paragraph 62; add a new section and paragraphs as follows: “Historic heritage needs more clarity and greater recognition of landowner rights Changes sought: 63. That listing of historic heritage on private land is by consent only; and private landowners have the right to reject a land use plan heritage listing on their property and for this to be determinative. 64. Clarity is required whether council would retain the ability to impose heritage listing over areas of geographical spread such as a heritage precinct. If the bill retains such powers; the external impacts from a new development within the precinct should allow Council to exercise reasonable discretion in matters of economic; cultural; urban and other outcomes in whether those impacts are appropriate.”

finalClauses.text: Receive the information.
Approve the attached submission on the Planning Bill 2025 and Natural Environment Bill 2025.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.
Note that the Council completed consultation with the community in October - November 2024 on the:
Te Ngākau Development Plan and scenarios to guide the future development of the precinct; and
Options for the City to Sea Bridge and former Capital E sites.

Note officers have considered the potential impact of the Building (Earthquake-prone Buildings) Amendment Bill on the former Capital E building’s status and identified the following options for the City to Sea Bridge and former Capital E:
Option 1 (not recommended): Renewal of the bridge and closure of former Capital E as a public building ($12.5m).
Option 2 (recommended option): Renewal of the City to Sea Bridge and Reuse of former Capital E as a public building (cold shell - minor strengthening of former Capital E) ($15m).
Agree to proceed with Option 2: Renewal of the City to Sea Bridge and Reuse of former Capital E as a public building
recommendations.actionComment: The project has commenced and the bridge will close on August 24.

recommendations.text: Direct officers to progress securing a tenant for this space at the earliest practicable opportunity to avoid delays in occupation.
recommendations.actionComment: Experience Wellington has been engaged and their requirements have been accommodated, so they can use the Capital E as a new art gallery.

recommendations.text: Note that savings provided by the recommended option ($17m) and forecast completion costs across the wider Te Ngākau programme will provide the Council with approximately $24.6m savings.
Note budgets will be updated depending on the decision in this meeting and will be presented in the Quarterly/Annual Report.

decisions.title: Quarterly 1 Performance Report 2025-26
decisions.summary: This report to Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee provides performance information for Quarter one of Year Two (2025/26) of the 2024-34 LongTerm plan (LTP). The information in the quarterly report supports governance oversight and service delivery performance monitoring of: Budget performance; Strategic activity area performance e.g. delivery of key service performance indicators; and Key strategies and their action plans. This report also outlines requirements for budget changes for the current financial year; to ensure spend aligns with Officer’s delegated authority.

recommendations.text: Receive the Quarter one (Q1) Performance Report on the 2024-34 Long-term Plan (LTP).
Note:

The Wellington Zoo signalled a likely deficit in 2024/25 in the Q3 report in activity 2.6.1 Conservation Visitor Attactions. The end result was a deficit of $1.148m. Council chose to carry these deficits as a risk in approving the Zoo’s FY24/25 Statement of Intent.
recommendations.actionComment: The information was noted by the Committee.

recommendations.text: Approve:
To carry forward capital budget of $4.4m for the Sludge Facility (2.4.2 Sewage Treatment) from 2024/25 to 2026/27.
To carry forward capital budget of $0.1m for the St James Theatre lift (3.1.2 Takina Wellington Convention & Exhibition Centre) from 2024/25 to 2025/26.
To carry forward capital budget of $0.3m for HUP2 (5.2.4 Housing) from 2024/25 to 2026/27.
To carry forward capital budget of $0.3m for the Town Hall (6.2.3 Earthquake Risk Mitigation – Built Environment) from 2024/25 to 2025/26.
To carry forward capital budget of $0.3m for the City Consenting and Compliance Improvement Programme (6.2.1 Building Control & Facilitation) from 2024/25 to 2025/26.
To carry forward capital budget of $0.1m for the Laneways Programme (6.1.2 Spaces and Centres Devlopment) from 2024/25 to 2026/27.
To carry forward capital budget of $0.1m for the Harbour Quays Corridor (7.1.8 Lets Get Wellington Moving) from 2024/25 to 2026/27.
To carry forward capital budget of $0.1m for the Eastern Corridor (7.1.8 Lets Get Wellington Moving) from 2024/25 to 2027/28.
To carry forward capital budget of $0.7m for Te Matapihi (10.1.1 Organisational Projects) from 2024/25 to 2025/26.
To carry forward capital budget of $0.6m for Town Hall Annex (10.1.1 Organisational Projects) from 2024/25 to 2026/27.
To carry forward capital budget of $0.5m for Workplace Accommodation (10.1.1 Organisational Projects) from 2024/25 to 2025/26.
To carry forward capital budget of $0.7m for City Gallery Seismic Upgrade (10.1.1 Organisational Projects) from 2024/25 to 2025/26.

To bring forward capital budget of $4.8m for the Begonia House (2.1.2 Wellington Gardens) from 2027/28. This would be split over three years - $0.025m for 2024/25; $3.723m for 2025/26 and $1.039m for 2026/27.

To increase the capital and capital revenue budgets of the Wellington Zoo (2.6.1 Conservation Visitor Attactions) by $0.8m for 2025/26.

Recommend to Te Kaunihera o Pōneke | Council:
To approve the funding of Wellington Zoo’s 2024/25 deficit of $1.148m.

decisions.title: Golden Mile - Review options
decisions.summary: This paper seeks Council’s direction on the next steps for the Golden Mile Project; proposing an independent review given emerging and escalating risks associated with contract development for the Courtenay Place works.
relatedReports: Let's Get Wellington Moving - Golden Mile Single Stage Business Case
Let's Get Wellington Moving: Golden Mile and Thorndon Quay | Hutt Road Funding
Golden Mile Traffic Resolution and Detailed Design
Notice of Motion regarding the Golden Mile

recommendations.text: Receive the information.
Agree to pause the current negotiations for the construction contract for the Golden Mile Courtenay Place section while a review is undertaken into the project.

Requests officers to seek an independent review of the project (option 3) to determine the validity of whether the project remains strategically aligned considering changes in cost and risk; updated benefit cost ratio assessments; and which includes an analysis of short and longer term construction economic impacts to Wellington’s CBD.

Note that a review would validate; but not fundamentally change; the existing project’s objectives and benefits which would remain as a transport project with associated streetscape and amenity benefits.

Request that; the independent review also provide advice as to whether minor changes to the project scope; or descoping options could be achieved; within the existing funding envelope; whilst retaining 51% funding from the New Zealand Transport Agency.
Agree that any costs associated with Review Options 3 or 4 that are incurred in this financial year will be debt funded; unless those costs can be absorbed into current budgets.

Agree that any costs associated with Review Options 3 or 4 that will be incurred in this future financial years that can not reasonably be absorbed into budgets will need to be considered as part the 2026/27 annual plan and may have an impact on rates.
Note officers will report back to Committee with the outcome of the review for the Committee’s direction on next steps for the project.

amendments.text: Agree to pause the following projects until the Golden Mile Review is complete:
the Harbour Quays Project
the Dixon Street Cycleway Project

finalClauses.text: Receive the information.
Agree to pause the current negotiations for the construction contract for the Golden Mile Courtenay Place section while a review is undertaken into the project.

Requests officers to seek an independent review of the project (option 3) to determine the validity of whether the project remains strategically aligned considering changes in cost and risk; updated benefit cost ratio assessments; and which includes an analysis of short and longer term construction economic impacts to Wellington’s CBD.

Note that a review would validate; but not fundamentally change; the existing project’s objectives and benefits which would remain as a transport project with associated streetscape and amenity benefits.

Request that; the independent review also provide advice as to whether minor changes to the project scope; or descoping options could be achieved; within the existing funding envelope; whilst retaining 51% funding from the New Zealand Transport Agency.
Agree that any costs associated with Review Options 3 or 4 that are incurred in this financial year will be debt funded; unless those costs can be absorbed into current budgets.

Agree that any costs associated with Review Options 3 or 4 that will be incurred in this future financial years that can not reasonably be absorbed into budgets will need to be considered as part the 2026/27 annual plan and may have an impact on rates.
Note officers will report back to Committee with the outcome of the review for the Committee’s direction on next steps for the project.

decisions.title: 2025-2028 Triennium Councillors' Remuneration
decisions.summary: This report to Te Kaunihera o Pōneke | Council seeks a decision on the allocation of the pool specified by the Remuneration Authority (the Authority); for the remuneration of councillors; based on the governance structure for the 2025-2028 triennium.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.

Recommend the below remuneration proposal to the Remuneration Authority: Position Proposed new base salary (per annum) Total (per annum) Mayor $201;947 $201;947 Deputy Mayor $136;526 $136;526 3 x chair of committee of the whole $125;149 $125;149 1 x chair of Te Takere | Regulatory Processes Committee $125;149 $125;149 10 x councillors $113;772 $113;772 Total (pool) $1;774;842

Agree to the following short role descriptions for the deputy mayor; chair of committee of the whole; and chair of the Te Takere | Regulatory Process Committee: Deputy Mayor The Deputy Mayor will: a) Assist the mayor in carrying out the statutory and leadership role of the Mayor. b) If the Mayor is absent or incapacitated; perform all the responsibilities and duties; and exercise any powers of the Mayor (other than the powers under section 41A LGA 2002 and the role of Justice of the Peace). c) Lead and take responsibility for liaison with Councillors on matters of support for carrying out their governance role. d) Assist the Mayor in day-to-day administration. e) Ensure that the Mayor's view is conveyed to committee and other meetings when they are absent on Council business. The Deputy Mayor is authorised to approve elected member attendance at conferences or training and associated travel and accommodation within New Zealand. [refer to Terms of Reference and Delegations; page 32] Chair of Committee of the whole The Chair of a Committee of the whole will be responsible for presiding over one of the Committees of the whole; which have specific responsibilities in line with their area of focus. The Chair of a Committee of the whole will be (in association with the Deputy Chair; and the agreement of the Mayor) the Council spokesperson with respect to matters within the Committee’s area of focus. Chair of Te Takere | Regulatory Processes Committee The Chair of the Te Takere | Regulatory Processes Committee will be responsible for presiding over that committee of the part which has responsibilities in line with its area of focus. The Chair of the Te Takere | Regulatory Processes Committee will be (in association with the Deputy Chair; and the agreement of the Mayor) the Council spokesperson with respect to matters within the Committee’s area of focus.

recommendations.text: Receive the information.
Adopt the schedule of meetings for the Council and committees for the period of December 2025 to September 2028 (Attachment 1)
Add additional Ngā Toki Whakahaere | CCO Review and Appointments Subcommittee meetings on 10 December 2025; 19 November 2026 and 9 December 2026
Change the meeting on 11 December 2025 from a Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee to a Te Hoe Matua | City Strategy and Delivery Committee
Change the meeting on 17 Dec 2025 from a Te Rauawa | Social; Cultural and Environmental Committee to a Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee

Change the meeting on 21 May 2026 from Te Urungi Whakatupu Ōhanga | Economic Growth and Development Subcommittee to a Te Taurapa | Council Planning and Finance Committee
